first: गुरुर् अग्निर् द्विजातीनां वर्णानां ब्राह्मणो गुरुः ।
en: Fire is the teacher of the twice-born, the Brahmin is the teacher of all classes, the husband is the teacher of the wife, and a guest is to be honoured by everyone.
Just as gold is tested in four ways, by rubbing, cutting, heating and beating, so a person is tested in four ways: by giving, by character, by qualities and by deeds.
Fear danger only while it has not yet come; once it has come, face it and strike without hesitation.
Children born from the same womb and under the same star are still not alike in nature, just as the thorns of the jujube bush are all different.
One with no desire will not seek office, one with no lust will not care for adornment, one without skill cannot speak pleasingly, and one who speaks plainly is no cheat.
Fools hate the learned, the poor hate the rich, women of good family hate courtesans, and unlucky women resent the lucky.
Learning is lost through laziness, money is lost when it is in another's hands, a field sown with too little seed is lost, and an army without a leader is lost.
Learning is kept by practice, a family is kept by good conduct, a noble person is known by his qualities, and anger is seen in the eyes.

first: वित्तेन रक्ष्यते धर्मो विद्या योगेन रक्ष्यते ।
en: Religion is protected by wealth, learning by practice, a king by gentleness, and a home by a good wife.
Those who speak ill of the learning of the Vedas, of the scriptures, of good conduct and of peaceful people only bring suffering on themselves for nothing.
Giving removes poverty, good conduct removes misfortune, wisdom removes ignorance, and devotion removes fear.
There is no disease like desire, no enemy like delusion, no fire like anger, and no happiness greater than knowledge.
A person is born alone and dies alone; alone he reaps the good and bad of his deeds; alone he falls into hell, and alone he reaches the highest state.
To one who knows God, heaven is worth no more than straw; to the brave, life is straw; to one who has mastered his senses, a woman is straw; to one free of desire, the whole world is straw.

first: विद्या मित्रं प्रवासेषु भार्या मित्रं गृहेषु च ।
en: Learning is a friend when you travel, a wife is a friend at home, medicine is a friend to the sick, and good deeds are a friend after death.
Rain on the ocean is wasted, food given to one who is full is wasted, gifts to the rich are wasted, and a lamp in daylight is wasted.

first: नास्ति मेघसमं तोयं नास्ति चात्मसमं बलम् ।
en: There is no water like rain water, no strength like your own, no light like the eyes, and nothing dearer than grain.
The poor want wealth, animals want speech, humans want heaven, and the gods want freedom from rebirth.

first: स्त्येन धार्यते पृथ्वी स्त्येन तपते रविः ।
en: Truth holds up the earth, truth makes the sun shine, truth makes the wind blow; everything rests on truth.
Wealth is unsteady, breath is unsteady, life and home are unsteady; in this moving and unmoving world, only righteousness stays firm.

first: नराणां नापितो धूर्तः पक्षिणां चैव वायसः ।
en: Among men the barber is the cunning one, among birds the crow, among beasts the jackal, and among women the flower-seller.

first: जनिता चोपनेता च यस्तु विद्यां प्रयच्छति ।
en: These five are counted as fathers: the one who gives birth, the one who performs the sacred-thread ceremony, the one who teaches, the one who gives food, and the one who protects from fear.

first: राजपत्नी गुरोः पत्नी मित्र पत्नी तथैव च ।
en: These five are counted as mothers: the king's wife, the teacher's wife, a friend's wife, one's wife's mother, and one's own mother.
